programme.title: The Boxing Day Tsunami
programme.desc: On December 26, 2004, the second day of Christmas, a devastating tsunami hit Indonesia and Thailand.It was the largest disaster of this type in history, and its dramatic effects were also felt in other parts of the world.It started with an earthquake under the Indian Ocean.A few minutes later, a hundred-meter wall of water broke through Indonesia.Then the tsunami reached Thailand, where it left unimaginable destruction in its wake.Scientists analyze the course of these tragic events and explain the connection between the earthquake and the subsequent tsunami.Rescuers give accounts of the fierce fight to save human lives, and survivors recall their losses in a tragedy that is difficult to recover from even after many years.

programme.title: Life Below Zero
programme.desc: Alaska has extremely harsh climatic conditions.Temperatures there regularly drop to life-threatening levels.Despite this, the region is inhabited by people.The tenth season of the program presents the everyday adventures of the inhabitants of four households from different parts of the Alaskan wilderness.Their lives focus primarily on hunting and careful preparations for and struggles with the long and frosty winter.Viewers will see, among others:Agnes Hailstone, who with her daughters tries to hunt caribou while her husband is away.

programme.desc: The creators of the series go on a train journey to various places around the world.During each expedition, they meet people who live in specific areas or work on the most unique railway routes.They will also discover the wonders of nature that can be admired from the train windows.They will talk to engineers responsible for maintaining the lines and historians who will talk about the circumstances of their construction and the difficulties their builders faced.Viewers will be able to admire the landscapes of Norway, New Zealand, Canada, Switzerland, Wales and Spain.

programme.title: Seven Worlds, One Planet
programme.desc: Antarctica is the coldest and windiest continent.The climate here is harsh, and only the toughest can survive.From Weddell seals crushing the ice with their teeth, to colorful starfish covering the seabed hidden under the ice.Penguin chicks may lose their lives when confronted by killer whales and leopard seals.Meanwhile, starfish and huge worms line the seabed as a feeding spectacle takes place on the surface.Life comes to Antarctica because the ocean surrounding the continent is extremely rich.Thousands of penguins, seals, albatrosses and over a hundred huge whales feast on the krill schools.Unfortunately, the local waters are warming, and as the temperature increases, the future of the local fauna and flora looks more and more uncertain.

programme.title: Penguins: Meet the Family
programme.desc: The penguin family includes as many as eighteen colorful species.Although the lush forests of New Zealand are not associated with these animals, this is where the penguin family evolved sixty million years ago and where most of its species live.One of the most interesting penguins is the great crested penguin, which loves bathing in spas.In turn, the African penguin has adapted to life in the city, which is why we can meet him walking among people on the streets of Cape Town.The Galapagos penguin managed to adapt to life in the hot equatorial climate.Penguins stand out for their parenting skills.Some species, such as white-eyed penguins, can travel long kilometers to find a suitable place to nest.Other species are clever - to repair their nests after winter, they steal stones from their neighbors' nests.

programme.title: Japan with Sue Perkins
programme.desc: British actress and comedian Sue Perkins travels around Japan.It is a country full of contrasts.Perkins begins his journey in Tokyo, inhabited by 36 million people.Characteristic features of this city are streets lit with digital neon lights and high-speed railways called bullet trains.Sue also goes to picturesque mountain villages where craftsmen cultivating ancient arts and customs work intently.The coexistence of tradition with modernity and the past with the future seems to be one of the reasons for the national pride of the people of Japan.
